config.description:
Configures {page}: its endpoints, model, system prompt, tools, display, style and every other setting. It runs lines of the KiSS CLI, one command per line; all lines of one call apply together or not at all, so batch related changes in a single call. Changes apply at once to the running configuration, and a call answers with what changed: the old line after -, the new one after +. The running configuration lasts until the page closes: copy running-config startup-config, or write memory, keeps it as what the page starts with, copy running-config <name> as a save, each once the user confirms it; copy <name> running-config goes back to a save, erase running-config back to the site defaults: offer to keep a change once it looks right.
Commands: set <module> <key> [name] <value> | no <module> <key> [name] | no <module> <name> | show <module> [key] [name] | show <module> <name> | show running-config [all] | show startup-config | show models | show css | show saves | show diff <config> <config> | copy <config> <config> | write [memory] | write erase | title <title> | show title | compact | show conversations | export [<id>|conversations|<config>] | import | erase <id>|conversations|<config>. A config is running-config, startup-config or a save by its name. show running-config lists what differs from the defaults, show running-config all every key with its default. title renames this conversation when the user asks; the conversation keeps its title, so a title needs no save. compact folds the history of this conversation into a summary before your next request, the last steps kept as written, when it grows long or the user asks. show conversations lists the conversations by id; export offers the user a file of this conversation, of another by its id, of the conversations, or of a config with its secrets, which reach the disk of the user and never you; import asks the user for a file and adds the conversations it holds that are not here yet, or runs the lines of a configuration as lines of the call; neither changes a conversation; erase removes a conversation by its id, the conversations but the pinned ones, or a config, once the user confirms it; each of these runs alone on its line.
A key is two fixed words, a module then a key; a key of a collection such as endpoints takes the item name next; the value always comes last. no <module> <name> removes a whole item of a collection, when the name is none of its keys. A line that stops short lists what may follow it: set lists the modules, set display its keys. show models lists the models of every endpoint, by endpoint, with their settings; set chat model takes a name as it lists it. Each model has its own request parameters, sent only when set: set models <temperature|top_p|top_k|min_p|max_tokens|presence_penalty|frequency_penalty|seed|reasoning_effort> <model> <value>, reasoning_effort being what the template of the model reads; set models compaction-trigger-tokens <model> <tokens> folds the history into a summary once a request holds that many, set models compaction-preserve-steps <model> <steps> the last steps it keeps as written. set tools max-rounds caps the tool rounds of a turn; set endpoints timeout <name> and set mcp timeout <name> give each server its seconds; set endpoints headers <name> 'Name: value; Name: value' and set mcp headers <name> send headers besides its key; set endpoints auth-header <name> 'api-key' or 'Authorization: Token' and set mcp auth-header <name> name the header that carries the key, the one of the protocol or a bearer token unless set. set display thinking|tool-calls closed, open or inference, open while the model writes them; set display rendering thinking|reply markdown or plain, plain in monospace as written; set display preview-argument <argument> names the argument every folded tool call shows, description by default, set tools preview-argument <tool> <argument> the one of a tool over it. An MCP server, set mcp url <name> <url> and its bearer set mcp key <name>, gives you its tools; a KiSS backend, itself an MCP server of the page whose config tool is <hostname>_server_config, holds routes that tool sets, set proxies url <name> <url> and set proxies key <name> there: set endpoints proxy <name> <backend> or set mcp proxy <name> <backend> here, <backend> the mcp item of that server, sends <name> through the route of the same name, its own url and key waiting unused, and no endpoints proxy <name> or no mcp proxy <name> sends it direct again; show tools lists every tool by who serves it; set tools use <name> off hides one, consent asks the user at each call, on lets it run. The page asks the user itself, with a card it shows as the line runs, whatever needs their consent: a change that opens a way out, the url or the proxy of an endpoint or an MCP server and opening a tool, every time, an erase or a copy that replaces a configuration; so run the line and let the card ask, never ask the user in the chat first; a refused change stays refused, never reach it another way. A new url takes the key of its item with it once the user agrees. A key never shows: show writes ! <module> key <name> is set for one that is set, and no line for one that is not. To give a key, write the line without its value, set mcp key <name>: the user types it in a field of their own, so never ask them to paste a key in the chat. A secret reads <removed> in the lines kept: it is not a value, never write it. set style <token> <value> sets a token of the page: show style lists them with their defaults, each a color, a length or a font; bg, fg and accent set a whole theme, every other color derived from them. show css lists the CSS of the page by component, a rule of a component carrying its class, svelte-composer for the composer, so a selector read there aims at that component alone; set style sheet <name> <css> restyles anything over it, the sheets applied by name, so one sheet holds one change. Words abbreviate while only one word starts so (sh run). Filter any output as IOS does, | include, exclude, begin or count <pattern>, the pattern the rest of the line, a regular expression minding case, count telling how many lines match: show running-config all | include ^set (tools|style). Quote values holding blanks.
Example call:
set style accent 'oklch(0.62 0.21 300)'
set endpoints url local http://localhost:9931/v1
set endpoints proxy hf backend
show style

description.description: Why I'm configuring the page, written first

compaction.ask: Summarize this conversation so that you can go on with it from the summary alone, in the language of the user: what the user asks now, in their own words, first; then their earlier requests, what was decided and done, what the tools found that still matters (paths, names, values, commands, errors) and what is left to do. Write only the summary and call no tool.
